What to say: State that 659 Columbus Ave is an existing restaurant approved by CUA in 1995, expanded by CUA in 2009, and now proposes to enlarge from 1,486 to 2,820 sq ft. Ask whether the North Beach Special Use District rule that a new restaurant 'will not enlarge the space' applies to this further expansion of an already-approved restaurant, and if so, whether any exception, variance or legislative relief is available. outcomes.original: Estimated time: 0 to 0 days. Estimated government cost: $0 to $0. Notes: No timeline or cost is given because the zoning determination concludes that enlarging the restaurant space is not permitted under Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) in the North Beach Special Use District. The rule states a new restaurant may be approved by Conditional Use only if it will not enlarge the space; the proposal increases floor area from 1,486 to 2,820 sq ft, so the no-enlargement condition is not met. The pathway analysis confirms the status is 'not permitted' due to this rule. Before any timeline or cost can be estimated, the operator must obtain written confirmation from San Francisco Planning Department on whether this rule applies to further expansion of a restaurant already approved and expanded by prior CUAs, and if so, whether any exception, variance or legislative relief is available. If Planning confirms the enlargement is allowed, the entitlement path would be: (1) Conditional Use Authorization, estimated 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 in filing fees depending on construction cost, though the comparables show 4.5 to 11 months for restaurant CUAs in this district; (2) Building permit with plan check and inspections, 14–120 days and $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation; (3) DPH plan check, 21–60 days and $828–$2,500 ($2,207 for a new restaurant); (4) Health permit to operate, 14–45 days and $470–$1,000 ($470 application fee). State and local business registration and certifications add 1–35 days and about $300–$1,200 in total fees. The critical path is the CUA hearing, which can take 6–10 months if the zoning conflict is resolved in the applicant's favor.
